newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Fields drying out slowly.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Fields drying out slowly.

text.p: Rains subsided across most areas the U.S. Northern Plains but spring wheat harvest remained slow as producers waited for fields to dry out, several cash grain dealers said.
"We're trying to cut grain in between some of the rain storms coming through, and it's been a very, very slow day," a northern Montana dealer said.
A southern Montana dealer said showers had let up but overnight rains of 0.25 inch left fields too wet for harvesting. In North Dakota, a few light sprinkles were reported Tuesday afternoon.
Cash bids were mixed with some locations quoting lower basis values in response to weak export demand at the Pacific Northwest. MGE spring wheat futures closed higher.

The U.S. Agriculture Department said Monday that the spring wheat harvest was 22 percent complete as of Sunday, below the 29 percent level of a year ago but just slightly behind the five-year average of 23 percent.
